source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Add'l Cov. E.5

q: A thief steals an HO-3 insured's credit card and charges $2,000 to it. Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms, the Credit Card, Electronic Fund Transfer Card or Access Device, Forgery and Counterfeit Money additional coverage pays up to:
choices: $200, after the deductible
$500, with no deductible
$1,000, after the deductible
$2,000, with no deductible
explain: This additional coverage pays up to $500, and no deductible applies. It does not cover use of the card by a resident of the household, by a person who was entrusted with the card, or in a business.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Add'l Cov. E.6
note: the 2022 forms removed this additional coverage. It is now added by endorsement HO 04 53, which pays up to the limit shown in its schedule.

q: A homeowners association charges each member an assessment after a covered windstorm damages the association's clubhouse. Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms (HO-3), the Section I Loss Assessment additional coverage pays up to:
choices: 10% of Coverage A
explain: The policy pays up to $1,000 for the insured's share of a loss assessment charged by a corporation or association of property owners, when the assessment results from direct loss to collectively owned property caused by a peril insured under Coverage A.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Add'l Cov. E.7
note: the 2022 forms pay up to $2,000.

q: Under the Collapse additional coverage of the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms (HO-3), an abrupt collapse of the dwelling is covered when it is caused by:
choices: Flood water that undermines and washes out the foundation
An earthquake that shakes the dwelling off its foundation
Decay that was hidden from view and unknown to the insured
Gradual settling, cracking and shrinking of the foundation over time
explain: The collapse coverage applies to an abrupt collapse caused by the Coverage C perils, hidden decay, hidden insect damage, weight of contents or people, weight of rain that collects on a roof, or defective materials or methods used in construction, remodeling or renovation, if the collapse happens during that work. Flood and earth movement remain excluded.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Add'l Cov. E.8

q: An HO-3 insured rents out a furnished apartment in her home. Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms, the Landlord's Furnishings additional coverage pays up to $2,500 for her appliances and furnishings in that apartment for loss by the Coverage C perils other than:
choices: Fire or lightning
Windstorm or hail
Theft
Vandalism or malicious mischief
explain: Landlord's furnishings in each apartment on the residence premises regularly rented or held for rental are covered up to $2,500 for the perils insured against under Coverage C, other than theft.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Add'l Cov. E.10
note: the 2022 forms raise the landlord's furnishings limit from $2,500 to $3,000. Theft is still the peril left out.

q: Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms (HO-3), the Grave Markers additional coverage pays up to what amount for grave markers and mausoleums damaged by a Coverage C peril?
explain: The policy pays up to $5,000 for grave markers, including mausoleums, on or away from the residence premises, for loss caused by a peril insured against under Coverage C.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Add'l Cov. E.12

q: An HO-3 insured's dog bites a child at a public park. Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms, Coverage F - Medical Payments to Others applies to the child's medical expenses:
choices: Only if a court first finds the insured legally liable for the injury
Only if the bite happened on the insured location
Because the injury was caused by an animal owned by an insured
Not at all, because injuries caused by an insured's animals are excluded
explain: Away from the insured location, Coverage F applies when the injury is caused by an animal owned by or in the care of an insured, by an insured's activities, by a residence employee in the course of employment, or by a condition on the insured location. Coverage F does not depend on the insured being legally liable.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Coverage F

sub: Section II - Coverage E and F
q: Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms (HO-3), the Coverage E limit shown in the Declarations is the most the insurer will pay for damages from:
choices: Each person injured in any one occurrence, with no limit on the total
Each insured who is sued, so two insureds double the amount available
Any one occurrence, whatever the number of insureds, claims or injured persons
All occurrences during the policy period combined, as an annual aggregate limit
explain: The Coverage E limit applies to all damages from any one occurrence, and it is the same regardless of the number of insureds, claims made or persons injured. Coverage F is a limit for each person in one accident.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Cond. A

q: The Severability of Insurance condition in Section II of the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms means that:
choices: Each insured has a separate Coverage E limit, so the limits can be added together
The insurance applies separately to each insured, without increasing the limit
Section II can be cancelled separately from Section I by either party
Each claimant's damages are subject to a separate limit for each occurrence
explain: The insurance applies separately to each insured, so one insured's conduct does not by itself take coverage away from another. The condition does not increase the insurer's limit of liability for any one occurrence.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Cond. B

q: Under the Claim Expenses additional coverage in Section II of the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms (HO-3), the insurer pays an insured's actual loss of earnings for helping with the defense at the insurer's request, up to:
choices: $50 a day
$100 a day
$200 a day
$250 a day
explain: Claim expenses include reasonable expenses an insured incurs at the insurer's request, including actual loss of earnings up to $250 per day, for assisting in the investigation or defense of a claim or suit.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Add'l Cov. A

q: Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms (HO-3), the Damage to Property of Others additional coverage pays, at replacement cost, up to:
choices: $250 per occurrence
$500 per occurrence
$1,000 per occurrence
$2,500 per occurrence
explain: The policy pays, at replacement cost, up to $1,000 per occurrence for property damage to property of others caused by an insured. It does not cover damage caused intentionally by an insured who is 13 or older, or damage to property owned by an insured.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Add'l Cov. C
note: the 2022 forms pay up to $5,000 per occurrence.

q: In Section II of the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms (HO-3), claim expenses and first aid expenses are paid:
choices: As part of the Coverage E limit
As part of the Coverage F limit
In addition to the limits of liability
Only after the Coverage E limit is used up
explain: The Section II additional coverages (claim expenses, first aid expenses, damage to property of others and loss assessment) are paid in addition to the limits of liability.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Additional Coverages

q: The 16-year-old son of an HO-3 insured mows neighbors' lawns for pay during the summer, working for himself with no employees. He negligently breaks a customer's window. Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms, Coverage E:
choices: Does not apply, because any activity an insured does for pay falls under the business exclusion
Applies, because the business exclusion excepts a self-employed insured under 21 with no employees
Applies only if the son's lawn-mowing income was no more than $2,000 in the 12 months before the policy period
Applies only if the Business Pursuits endorsement has been added to the policy
explain: The Section II business exclusion does not apply to an insured under the age of 21 who is involved in a part-time or occasional, self-employed business with no employees.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Excl. E.2
note: the $2,000 figure in one choice is the 2011 business threshold; the 2022 forms use $5,000. The under-21 exception, the answer here, is in both editions.

q: An HO-3 named insured owns a 14-foot fishing boat powered by a 20-horsepower outboard motor. He negligently injures a swimmer while operating it. Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms, Coverage E - Personal Liability:
choices: Applies, because the outboard motor is 25 horsepower or less
Does not apply, because all owned watercraft are excluded
Applies only if the boat was declared to the insurer at policy inception
Applies only while the boat is stored on the residence premises
explain: The watercraft liability exclusion does not apply to watercraft powered by one or more outboard engines or motors with 25 total horsepower or less. Owned outboards of more than 25 horsepower are covered only if acquired during the policy period, or declared or reported as the form requires.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Excl. B.2

q: The 12-year-old daughter of an HO-3 named insured lives in the household and is hurt when her father negligently backs a riding mower into her. Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms, a liability claim against the father for her injury is:
choices: Covered under Coverage E, up to the limit shown in the Declarations
Covered under Coverage E, but only for her reasonable medical expenses
Not covered, because Coverage E excludes bodily injury to an insured
Not covered, because a riding mower is a motor vehicle
explain: Coverage E excludes bodily injury to you or to an insured, and a resident relative is an insured. Coverage F does not apply to regular residents of the household either.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Excl. F; Sec. II Coverage F

q: An HO-3 insured leaves for a two-month winter vacation, turns off the furnace and does not drain the plumbing. A pipe freezes and bursts, damaging the dwelling. Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms, the loss is:
choices: Covered, because the HO-3 insures the dwelling against any loss that is not excluded
Covered, but only for the cost of tearing out and replacing the broken pipe
Not covered, because she neither maintained heat nor shut off and drained the water
Not covered, because freezing of plumbing is never covered under an HO-3
explain: Loss from freezing of a plumbing or heating system is not covered unless the insured used reasonable care to maintain heat in the building or to shut off the water supply and drain the systems and appliances.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Perils Insured Against A.2

q: During a storm, rain blows in through a window an HO-3 insured left open and ruins a rug. The building itself is not damaged. Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms, the loss to the rug (Coverage C) is:
choices: Covered under the windstorm or hail peril, because wind drove the rain into the house
Covered under the accidental discharge or overflow of water peril
Not covered, because wind or hail did not first make an opening in the building
Not covered, because rugs and carpets are excluded property
explain: The windstorm or hail peril does not include loss to property inside a building caused by rain, snow, sleet, sand or dust unless the direct force of wind or hail damages the building, causing an opening in a roof or wall through which it enters.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Perils Insured Against B.2

q: The daughter of an HO-3 insured is a full-time student living in a college dormitory. Her laptop is stolen from her dorm room. Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms, the theft is covered if she has been at the dormitory at any time during the:
choices: 30 days before the loss
45 days before the loss
60 days before the loss
90 days before the loss
explain: Theft from another residence owned by, rented to or occupied by an insured is not covered unless the insured is temporarily living there. A student's property is covered at the residence the student occupies to attend school if the student has been there at any time during the 90 days before the loss.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Perils Insured Against B.9

q: Thieves steal copper pipe and lumber from a house being built for an HO-3 insured before it is finished and occupied. Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms, the theft is:
choices: Covered under Coverage A as materials and supplies for use in the construction
Covered, but only up to the limit for theft away from the residence premises
Not covered, because theft in or to a dwelling under construction is excluded
Not covered, because theft is never a covered cause of loss under Coverage A
explain: Coverages A and B do not insure theft in or to a dwelling under construction, or theft of materials and supplies for use in the construction, until the dwelling is finished and occupied.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Perils Insured Against A.2

q: Squirrels nest in the attic of an HO-3 dwelling and chew through the roof decking. Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms, the damage to the dwelling is:
choices: Covered, because Coverage A is written on an open-perils basis with no exclusions
Covered under the vandalism or malicious mischief peril
Not covered, because loss caused by birds, rodents or insects is excluded
Not covered, because the attic is not part of the dwelling
explain: Open-perils coverage on the dwelling still has exclusions. Coverages A and B do not insure loss caused by birds, rodents or insects, and squirrels are rodents.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Perils Insured Against A.2

q: A storm knocks down a utility line several miles from an HO-3 insured's home. The home loses power for three days and the food in the freezer spoils; nothing on the residence premises is damaged. Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms, the spoiled food is:
choices: Covered as a direct loss by windstorm, because a storm brought down the utility line
Covered, because power failure is a named peril under Coverage C
Not covered, because the power failure took place off the residence premises
Not covered, because food is excluded property under Coverage C
explain: Section I excludes loss caused by the failure of power or other utility service if the failure takes place off the residence premises. If the failure leads to a loss from a covered peril on the residence premises, that resulting loss is covered.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Excl. A.4

q: To keep a fire from spreading, the fire department orders an HO-3 insured's detached garage torn down. Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms, the loss of the garage is:
choices: Excluded as governmental action, because a public authority ordered it
Excluded under the ordinance or law exclusion
Covered, if a loss by fire would be covered under the policy
Covered only up to 10% of the Coverage B limit
explain: The governmental action exclusion does not apply to acts ordered by a governmental or public authority at the time of a fire to prevent its spread, if the loss caused by fire would be covered under the policy.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Excl. A.9

q: A single loss under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms (HO-3) is subject to two different deductibles. How do they apply?
choices: Both deductibles are subtracted from the loss
Only the lower deductible applies
Only the highest deductible applies
The two deductibles are averaged
explain: If two or more deductibles under the policy apply to a loss, only the highest deductible amount applies.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Cond. B

q: After a burglary, the Duties After Loss condition of the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms (HO-3) requires the insured to give prompt notice to the insurer or its agent and to notify:
choices: The Department of Insurance and Financial Services
The police
The mortgagee
The local fire department
explain: In case of loss by theft, the insured must notify the police. For a credit card or electronic fund transfer card loss, the insured must also notify the card company.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Cond. C
note: the duty to notify the card company is in the 2011 forms only. The 2022 forms dropped it when the credit card coverage moved to endorsement HO 04 53. Notifying the police is required in both.

q: A covered fire destroys a six-year-old sofa in the home of an insured with an unendorsed HO-3 under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms. The sofa is paid for at:
choices: Replacement cost, with no deduction for depreciation, once it is replaced
Actual cash value, but not more than the cost to repair or replace it
Its original purchase price, as shown on the receipt
80% of the cost to replace it with a new sofa of like kind and quality
explain: Personal property, awnings, carpeting, household appliances, outdoor equipment and structures that are not buildings are settled at actual cash value at the time of loss, but not more than the amount required to repair or replace. Replacement cost on personal property requires an endorsement.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Cond. D.1

q: An HO-3 insured settles a dwelling loss on an actual cash value basis. Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms, she can still claim the additional amount due on a replacement cost basis if she notifies the insurer of her intent to repair or replace within:
choices: 30 days after the loss
60 days after the loss
180 days after the loss
1 year after the loss
explain: The insured may disregard the replacement cost provisions and claim on an actual cash value basis, then make a further claim for the additional replacement cost amount if she notifies the insurer within 180 days after the date of loss of her intent to repair or replace the damaged building.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Cond. D.2.e

q: One of a pair of antique candlesticks owned by an HO-3 insured is destroyed in a covered fire. Under the Loss to a Pair or Set condition of the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms, the insurer may repair or replace the lost piece to restore the pair, or pay:
choices: The full value of the pair, after taking the remaining candlestick as salvage
Half the value of the pair, because one of the two pieces was lost
The difference in the pair's actual cash value before and after the loss
Nothing, because a pair or set is covered only if it is specifically scheduled
explain: For a loss to a pair or set, the insurer may repair or replace any part to restore the pair or set to its value before the loss, or pay the difference between the actual cash value of the property before and after the loss.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Cond. E

q: Under the Our Option condition of the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms (HO-3), the insurer may repair or replace damaged property with material of like kind and quality if it gives the insured written notice within:
choices: 10 days after the loss
30 days after it receives the signed, sworn proof of loss
60 days after it receives the signed, sworn proof of loss
90 days after the loss
explain: If the insurer gives written notice within 30 days after it receives the insured's signed, sworn proof of loss, it may repair or replace any part of the damaged property with material or property of like kind and quality.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Cond. I

q: Under the Mortgage Clause of the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms (HO-3), if the insurer decides to cancel or not renew the policy, the mortgagee named in the policy is notified at least:
choices: 10 days before the cancellation or nonrenewal takes effect
20 days before the cancellation or nonrenewal takes effect
30 days before the cancellation or nonrenewal takes effect
60 days before the cancellation or nonrenewal takes effect
explain: Under the unendorsed ISO mortgage clause, the mortgagee is notified at least 10 days before the date a cancellation or nonrenewal takes effect.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Cond. L

q: A moving company damages an HO-3 insured's furniture and argues that the insured's homeowners policy should pay instead of the mover. Which Section I condition of the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms prevents the mover from benefiting from the policy?
choices: Abandonment of Property
Recovered Property
No Benefit to Bailee
Our Option
explain: Under No Benefit to Bailee, the insurer will not recognize any assignment or grant any coverage that benefits a person or organization holding, storing or moving property for a fee.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Cond. M

q: The insurer pays an HO-3 insured for a stolen painting, and the police later recover it. Under the Recovered Property condition of the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms:
choices: The painting belongs to the insurer, and the insured has no choice in the matter
The insured must take the painting back and repay the full loss payment
The insured chooses: take the painting back, or let the insurer keep it
The painting must be sold and the proceeds divided equally between them
explain: If property the insurer has paid for is recovered, at the insured's option it is returned to or kept by the insured, or it becomes the insurer's property. If the insured keeps it, the loss payment is adjusted.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Conditions, Recovered Property

q: An HO-3 insured is sued for a covered injury and then files for bankruptcy. Under the Section II conditions of the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms, the insurer:
choices: Is released from its obligations to the insured and the claimant
Is not relieved of its obligations under the policy
Owes the claimant only half of any judgment
May cancel the policy back to its inception date
explain: Bankruptcy of an insured does not relieve the insurer of its obligations under the policy.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Cond. G

q: Under the Liberalization Clause of the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms, a change that broadens coverage without additional premium applies to an existing policy automatically if the insurer implements it in the insured's state:
choices: At any time within 12 months before the policy period
Within 60 days before, or during, the policy period
Only at the policy's next renewal
Only if the insured asks for it in writing
explain: A change that broadens coverage under the same edition of the policy without additional premium applies automatically as of the date the insurer implements it in the state, provided that date falls within 60 days before or during the policy period. The clause does not apply to changes made through a general program revision.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Secs. I and II Cond. A

q: Under the Subrogation condition of the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms, an insured may waive rights of recovery against another person:
choices: At any time, orally or in writing
In writing, before a loss
Only after the insurer has paid the loss
Never; any waiver voids the coverage
explain: An insured may waive in writing, before a loss, all rights of recovery against any person. If the rights are not waived, the insurer may require an assignment of them to the extent of its payment. Subrogation does not apply to Coverage F or to Damage to Property of Others.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Secs. I and II Cond. F

q: The named insured under a homeowners policy (2011 ISO forms) dies during the policy period. For the premises and property that were covered at the time of death, the policy:
choices: Ends at once, and any unearned premium is refunded to the estate
Continues only for a surviving spouse who lives in the home
Insures the legal representative of the deceased
Converts automatically to a dwelling policy
explain: If a person named in the Declarations dies, the insurer insures the legal representative of the deceased, but only for the premises and property of the deceased that were covered under the policy at the time of death.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Secs. I and II Cond. G

sub: Selected Endorsements - Limited Fungi, Wet or Dry Rot, or Bacteria
q: Under the 2002 ISO Limited Fungi, Wet or Dry Rot, or Bacteria Coverage endorsement for the HO-3, the Coverage E amount shown in the schedule is:
choices: Paid in addition to the Coverage E limit for each occurrence during the policy period
An aggregate sublimit that is part of, not in addition to, the Coverage E limit
A separate limit that applies to each person injured
A deductible the insured pays before Coverage E applies
explain: The schedule shows a Section I amount for the property coverage and a Coverage E aggregate sublimit for liability. The Coverage E amount is within the Coverage E limit; it does not add to it.
source: ISO HO 04 27 04 02, Schedule; PF&M Analysis: ISO Homeowners Optional Coverage Endorsements (July 2014)

q: Under the 2000 ISO Earthquake endorsement for homeowners policies, the earthquake deductible is a percentage of:
choices: The amount of the earthquake loss, before any other deductible
The Coverage A or Coverage C limit, whichever is greater
The total of the Coverage A, B, C and D limits
The market value of the dwelling at the time of the loss
explain: The earthquake deductible is the percentage shown in the schedule multiplied by the Coverage A or Coverage C limit, whichever is greater. It replaces the regular Section I deductible for earthquake losses.

q: Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners program, the Scheduled Personal Property endorsement insures the scheduled articles:
choices: For the Coverage C named perils, subject to the policy deductible
On an open-perils basis, with no deductible
For theft only, subject to a $250 deductible
For fire and theft only, while on the residence premises
explain: The endorsement covers the scheduled classes of property, such as jewelry, furs, cameras, musical instruments, silverware, golfer's equipment, fine arts, stamps and coins, against risks of direct physical loss, worldwide, with no deductible.
source: PF&M Analysis: HO 04 61 Scheduled Personal Property Endorsement (July 2017)

sub: Selected Endorsements - Personal Property Replacement Cost
q: Under the 2011 ISO Personal Property Replacement Cost endorsement, the insurer pays no more than actual cash value until the property is actually repaired or replaced when the cost to repair or replace is more than:
explain: If the cost to repair or replace is more than $500, the insurer pays no more than the actual cash value until the repair or replacement is complete. The insured may claim actual cash value first and then claim the additional amount by giving notice within 180 days after the loss.
note: the 2022 edition of this endorsement (HO 04 90 03 22) uses $1,000.

q: A homeowner cares for a neighbor's child twice a week, and in return the neighbor cares for hers. No money changes hands. Under the 2011 ISO Homeowners forms, this arrangement is:
choices: A business, so any liability arising from it is excluded under Section II
Not a business, because it is a mutual exchange of home day care services
A business, unless the Home Day Care Coverage endorsement is attached to the policy
Not a business only if each child is a relative of the insured
explain: The definition of "business" excepts home day care services for which no compensation is received other than the mutual exchange of such services, and home day care provided to a relative of an insured. Paid day care for others is a business and needs the Home Day Care endorsement.
source: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Definitions B.3; PF&M Analysis: ISO Homeowners Optional Coverage Endorsements (July 2014), HO 04 97
note: in the 2022 program the endorsement is titled Limited Home Day Care Coverage. The mutual-exchange exception is in both editions.

q: A schoolteacher adds the Business Pursuits endorsement to her homeowners policy. The endorsement can also be written to cover her liability for:
choices: Corporal punishment of pupils
Professional errors in grading and testing
Damage to school property in her care
Injury to fellow teachers on the job
explain: The Business Pursuits endorsement covers an insured's liability from business activities when the insured is not the owner or a partner of the business, such as a teacher, clerical worker or salesperson. For teachers, coverage for corporal punishment of pupils can be added.
source: PF&M Analysis: ISO Homeowners Optional Coverage Endorsements (July 2014), HO 24 71
note: in the 2022 program this endorsement (HO 24 71) is titled Designated Business Pursuits Liability Coverage.

q: The Personal Injury endorsement to a homeowners policy adds coverage for all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: Libel or slander
False arrest or malicious prosecution
Invasion of privacy
Bodily injury to a guest
explain: The endorsement adds coverage for offenses such as false arrest, detention or imprisonment, malicious prosecution, libel, slander, defamation, invasion of privacy and wrongful eviction or entry. Bodily injury to a guest is already the subject of Coverage E and Coverage F; it is not a personal injury offense.
source: PF&M Analysis: ISO Homeowners Optional Coverage Endorsements (July 2014), HO 24 82

q: Under the 2022 ISO Homeowners forms, a paid activity other than the insured's trade, profession or occupation is not a "business" if no insured received more than what total compensation for it in the 12 months before the policy period?
explain: The 2022 "business" definition excepts activities for which no insured receives more than $5,000 in total compensation in the 12 months before the policy period. The 2011 forms used $2,000, which is why $2,000 is the tempting wrong answer here. Volunteer work, home day care done as a mutual exchange of services, and home day care for a relative are excepted in both editions.
source: ISO HO 00 03 03 22, Definitions B.3 (form text); ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Definitions B.3

sub: Section I - Coverage C Special Limits
q: A burglar steals $6,000 of jewelry from the home of an insured whose HO-3 is written on the 2022 ISO Homeowners forms. Ignoring the deductible, the policy will pay:
explain: The 2022 forms put a $2,000 special limit on loss by theft of jewelry, watches, furs, and precious and semiprecious stones. The 2011 forms used $1,500. In both editions the limit applies only to theft: jewelry destroyed by a covered fire is paid up to the Coverage C limit.
source: ISO HO 00 03 03 22, Sec. I Coverage C.3.e (form text)

sub: Section I - Coverage C Special Limits
q: A covered fire destroys $900 in cash kept in the home of an HO-3 insured. Under the 2022 ISO Homeowners forms, and ignoring the deductible, the policy will pay:
explain: The 2022 forms limit money, bank notes, coins and similar property to $300 per loss, whatever covered peril causes the loss. The 2011 forms used $200.
source: ISO HO 00 03 03 22, Sec. I Coverage C.3.a (form text)

sub: Section I - Coverage C Special Limits
q: Which special limit of liability in the 2022 ISO Homeowners policy (HO-3) is stated correctly?
choices: Theft of jewelry, watches and furs is limited to $1,500
Watercraft, including trailers and outboard motors, is limited to $1,500
Theft of firearms is limited to $3,000
Business property on the residence premises is limited to $2,500
explain: The 2022 special limits are: money $300; securities $2,000; watercraft $2,000; trailers $2,000; theft of jewelry $2,000; theft of firearms $3,000; theft of silverware $3,000; business property $3,000 on the residence premises and $1,500 away from it. The three wrong choices state the 2011 amounts.
source: ISO HO 00 03 03 22, Sec. I Coverage C.3.a-i (form text)

sub: Section I - Coverage C Special Limits
q: The 2022 ISO Homeowners forms added a Coverage C special limit of liability that the 2011 forms did not have. It applies to:
choices: Bicycles and their accessories
Musical instruments
Cameras and photo equipment
Model or hobby aircraft
explain: The 2022 forms add a $2,000 special limit on model or hobby aircraft (those not used or designed to carry people or cargo). The 2011 forms covered them as personal property with no special limit. Neither edition has a special limit for bicycles, musical instruments or cameras.
source: ISO HO 00 03 03 22, Sec. I Coverage C.3.l (form text); ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Coverage C.3 and C.4

q: A tenant insured under an HO-4 written on the 2022 ISO Homeowners forms has a $12,000 Coverage C limit. A covered fire destroys personal property he keeps in a rented self-storage unit. The most the policy will pay for that property is:
explain: Under the 2022 forms, property in a self-storage facility is limited to 10% of Coverage C or $1,500, whichever is greater. 10% of $12,000 is $1,200, so the $1,500 floor applies. Under the 2011 forms the floor was $1,000, and the answer would have been $1,200.
source: ISO HO 00 04 03 22, Sec. I Coverage C.2 (form text); ISO HO 00 03 03 22, Sec. I Coverage C.2 (form text)

q: A windstorm blows two of an HO-3 insured's trees onto her detached garage, damaging it. Hauling the trees away costs $1,800 for each tree. Under the 2022 ISO Homeowners forms, the tree removal provision pays:
explain: The 2022 forms pay up to $3,000 per loss to remove the insured's trees felled by windstorm or hail, or by weight of ice, snow or sleet, when a tree damages a covered structure or blocks a driveway or a ramp for a handicapped person. No more than $1,500 is paid for any one tree: $1,500 + $1,500 = $3,000. The 2011 forms paid $1,000 per loss and $500 per tree.
source: ISO HO 00 03 03 22, Sec. I Add'l Cov. E.1.b (form text)

q: Vandals destroy a mature ornamental tree worth $4,000 in the yard of an HO-3 insured whose Coverage A limit is $300,000. Under the 2022 ISO Homeowners forms, the Trees, Shrubs and Other Plants additional coverage pays up to:
explain: The 2022 forms cover trees, shrubs, plants and lawns up to 5% of the Coverage A limit ($15,000 here), but no more than $1,500 for any one tree, shrub or plant. The 2011 forms capped each at $500. Vandalism is one of the covered perils; windstorm is not.
source: ISO HO 00 03 03 22, Sec. I Add'l Cov. E.3 (form text)

q: Under the 2022 ISO Homeowners forms, coverage for unauthorized use of an insured's credit card is:
choices: A $500 additional coverage with no deductible
Not part of the form, but available by endorsement
A $1,000 additional coverage after the deductible
Included in the special limit on money
explain: The 2011 forms included a $500 additional coverage for credit card, electronic fund transfer card, forgery and counterfeit money losses. The 2022 forms removed it. The coverage is now added by endorsement HO 04 53, which pays up to the limit shown in its schedule.
source: ISO HO 00 03 03 22, Sec. I Additional Coverages E.1-11 (form text); ISO HO 04 53 03 22 (form text)

q: A homeowners association assesses each member after a covered windstorm damages the association's clubhouse. Under the 2022 ISO Homeowners forms (HO-3), the Section I Loss Assessment additional coverage pays up to:
explain: The 2022 forms pay up to $2,000 for the insured's share of a loss assessment charged by a corporation or association of property owners. The Section II loss assessment limit is also $2,000. The 2011 forms paid $1,000 under each.
source: ISO HO 00 03 03 22, Sec. I Add'l Cov. E.6 and Sec. II Add'l Cov. D (form text)

q: Under the 2022 ISO Homeowners forms (HO-3), the Landlord's Furnishings additional coverage pays, for each rented apartment on the residence premises, up to:
explain: The 2022 forms cover the insured's appliances, carpeting and other household furnishings in each apartment on the residence premises that is regularly rented or held for rental, up to $3,000, for the Coverage C perils other than theft. The 2011 forms paid $2,500.
source: ISO HO 00 03 03 22, Sec. I Add'l Cov. E.9 (form text)

q: Under the 2022 ISO Homeowners forms (HO-3), the insurer will settle a building loss at replacement cost before repair or replacement is complete if the cost to repair or replace is:
choices: Less than 5% of the insurance on the building and less than $2,500
Less than 10% of the insurance on the building, with no dollar test
Less than $5,000, with no percentage test
Less than 5% of the insurance on the building and less than $5,000
explain: Both tests must be met: the cost must be less than 5% of the amount of insurance on the building and less than $5,000. Otherwise the insurer pays no more than actual cash value until repair or replacement is complete. The 2011 forms used $2,500 for the dollar test.
source: ISO HO 00 03 03 22, Sec. I Cond. D.2.d (form text)

q: Under the 2022 ISO Homeowners forms (HO-3), the Damage to Property of Others additional coverage pays, at replacement cost, up to:
choices: $500 per occurrence
$1,000 per occurrence
$2,500 per occurrence
$5,000 per occurrence
explain: The 2022 forms pay, at replacement cost, up to $5,000 per occurrence for property damage to property of others caused by an insured. The 2011 forms paid $1,000. In both editions there is no coverage for damage caused intentionally by an insured who is 13 or older, or for property owned by an insured.
source: ISO HO 00 03 03 22, Sec. II Add'l Cov. C (form text)

q: Under the 2022 ISO Earthquake endorsement for homeowners policies, the deductible is a percentage of the Coverage A or Coverage C limit, whichever is greater, but not less than:
explain: The deductible is found by multiplying the greater of the Coverage A or Coverage C limit by the percentage shown in the schedule, and it cannot be less than $500. The 2000 edition's minimum was $250.
source: ISO HO 04 54 03 22 (form text); ISO HO 04 54 10 00 (form text)

q: In the 2022 ISO Homeowners program, a teacher who wants Section II coverage for liability arising out of her teaching job would add:
choices: Designated Business Pursuits Liability Coverage
Permitted Incidental Occupancies - Residence Premises
Home Business Insurance Coverage
Personal Injury Coverage
explain: HO 24 71 is titled Designated Business Pursuits Liability Coverage in the 2022 program; earlier programs called it Business Pursuits. It applies Coverages E and F to the business pursuits of the insured named in it, but not to a business the insured owns or financially controls, and it can be written to cover corporal punishment by a teacher.
source: ISO HO 24 71 03 22 (form text)
